lede: Shaka Guide is worth it for most people driving the Road to Hana, a Hawaiian island loop or a big national park on their own: its apps rate 4.8 to 4.9 out of 5 on the App Store from more than 49,000 ratings, and a tour costs less than a meal. Here's how it works, what reviewers praise and complain about, and what it costs.

parts: Shaka Guide is a legitimate Hawaii company that has sold self-guided audio tours since 2016. Its tours play stories, music and directions by GPS as you drive or walk, and work offline once downloaded. Reviewers mostly love the storytelling; the complaints are about narration running ahead of or behind where you are, closed stops, and some tours feeling more like directions than history.

The app is free. You buy tours, one at a time or in bundles, on shakaguide.com or in the app. The site listed 106 tours on November 22, 2026: 21 in Hawaii, 55 in national parks, 36 scenic drives and 17 walking tours (some count in more than one group).

parts: Of the 100 most recent reviews of the main app and the Maui app on the App Store, 90 were five stars. Reviewers praise the stories and music, directions that keep working with no cell signal, and being able to stop wherever they like instead of following a bus tour.

The complaints are worth knowing. One Big Island bundle buyer found it too focused on directions and short on history. Others said the narration played ahead of where they were, cut off and picked back up confusingly, or that some stops were closed. One Maui reviewer said they missed the waterfalls they hoped to see. Most of these issues are easier to avoid if you download the tour over Wi-Fi first and start it at the suggested starting point.

Yes. Shaka Guide LLC is the seller named on its App Store apps, says it opened in 2016 and is rooted in Hawaii, and names its team, including its two co-founders, on its About page. It lists a support phone number with office hours in Hawaii time, a chat and an email address, and publishes its terms, privacy policy and an FAQ on downloads and refunds. Purchases go through a normal checkout, and your receipt carries a redeem code for the app.

For one big drive, a single tour of $15 to $25 costs less than a guided bus seat for one person, and covers the whole car. If you'll take two tours or more on one island, the $34.99 bundle is the better deal: the Maui bundle's six tours cost $124.94 bought one by one.

It's less worth it if you mainly want deep history at every stop, or if you won't download the tour in advance. A promo code takes {pct} off on top for website orders. parts: Shaka Guide suits families and couples renting a car in Hawaii or visiting national parks who want a guide's stories without a fixed schedule. It suits less those who want a live guide to answer questions, those relying on Android Auto, or anyone who won't have Wi-Fi to download the tour before setting out.

faq: Is Shaka Guide legit?
Yes. Shaka Guide LLC, a Hawaii company selling audio tours since 2016, publishes its apps on the App Store, lists a phone number, chat and email for support, and publishes its terms and FAQ.
Is Shaka Guide worth it?

For most self-drive trips, yes: a tour costs $6.99 to $24.99 for the whole car, and island bundles cost $34.99 for 4 to 6 tours. Some reviewers wanted more history and found the narration out of step at times.
Is Shaka Guide worth it for Road to Hana?

Its Maui app rates 4.9 out of 5 from 24,516 App Store ratings (November 22, 2026), and the Classic Road to Hana tour covers 27 stops for $24.99. Download it over Wi-Fi before you leave, as cell service is patchy along the road.
What is Shaka Guide's rating?

On the US App Store, the main Shaka Guide app rates 4.9 out of 5 from 15,538 ratings, and the Maui app 4.9 from 24,516. Shaka Guide's own site shows 4.9 from 111,088 ratings. It has no Trustpilot page.
Does Shaka Guide work without cell service?
Yes, once the tour is downloaded. Shaka Guide says the map, audio and directions work offline using your phone's GPS; only articles need a connection.
Does Shaka Guide work with Android Auto or CarPlay?
It works with Apple CarPlay. Its FAQ says it doesn't work with Android Auto yet, so Android users play it from the phone or through the car stereo by cable or Bluetooth.
What does Shaka Guide offer?

106 self-guided audio tours: Hawaii island drives, national parks such as Yellowstone, Zion and the Grand Canyon, scenic drives like the Blue Ridge Parkway, and walking tours in cities such as Boston and Honolulu.
Where is Shaka Guide based?
Shaka Guide says it is rooted in Hawaii, where it started in 2016, and its support hours are given in Hawaii time.
Can I get a refund from Shaka Guide?
Its terms say payments are non-refundable except as the terms provide, and that refunds under its money-back satisfaction guarantee are at its discretion. Contact support first.
